name: Ceat Ltd
title: Ceat Ltd - 500878 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: CEAT standalone revenue grew 18.2% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR4,036 crore, with standalone EBITDA of INR587 crore; Q1 FY27 faces raw material costs up about 15%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter, with standalone revenue up 18.2% YoY and standalone EBITDA margin expanding 299 bps YoY to about 14.6%, helped by the GST cut on tyres. FY26 standalone revenue grew 15.5% to INR15,215 crore and EBITDA crossed INR2,000 crore for the first time. Management now guides to a sharp raw material cost increase in Q1 FY27 (about 15%, possibly near 20% by end-Q1) driven by crude near $107/bbl, higher natural rubber and a weaker rupee. It is pushing price hikes of about 10% in replacement and staggered hikes in OEM and international business, and expects demand moderation as prices rise. CAMSO remains in transition, with customer interface targeted to be about 90% in-house by September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +299 bps YoY, +51 bps QoQ; margin about 14.6%
vs INR100.4 crore YoY and INR191.6 crore QoQ; after INR10 crore VRS exceptional

segments.name: Replacement
segments.commentary: Grew mid-teens in Q4; 2-wheeler grew mid-20s; truck/bus/farm low teens; PCUV mid-single digit. Price hikes of about 5% taken March-April, with another 5% planned in May-June.

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: Grew mid-teens in Q4 and over 20% in FY26; MHCV high double digit in Q4; passenger car very high growth with share in premium vehicles. Price index hike of low single digit on 1 April, with a heavier hike on 1 July.

segments.name: International Business
segments.commentary: Very strong Q4 across segments; saliency rose from 19% to 20.4% (above 23% including CAMSO); non-specialty grew high 20s; Middle East about 15% of business, near zero in Q4. Price increases of 3-5% taken, with a further 5% announced.

segments.name: CAMSO
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue flat QoQ and down about 5% vs Q3 due to local fuel shortage in Sri Lanka. Transition to be completed by March 2027; customer interface about 90% by September 2026; margin impact expected from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 raw material cost increase about 15%, could be near 20% by end-Q1; management says only a small portion can be offset by cost optimisation.
Replacement: total price hike of about 10% vs March targeted, with about 5% taken by April and the balance staggered in May-June.
MHCV replacement demand expected high single digit near term; truck-bus replacement may slow to low single digit after price hikes but not turn negative.
PCR replacement market expected to improve gradually from 1-2% to 3-5%; 2-wheeler replacement expected single to high single digit growth through FY27.
FY27 India capex (ex-CAMSO) of INR1,350-1,400 crore; CAMSO upstream capex about $20-25 million in addition, with the upstream facility ready by March 2027.
Debt kept around INR3,000 crore in Q1 FY27; may rise slightly in later quarters as capex steps up; management views current other income of INR62.5 crore as unsustainable.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at 85-90% across categories; management says planned utilisation is 90%-plus.
Q1 FY27 capex limited to mandatory spend of about INR200-250 crore; more growth capex to be scaled up once conditions normalise.
FY27 India capex about INR1,350-1,400 crore, about 25% above FY26's INR1,076 crore.
CAMSO upstream (mixers and calenders) to be ready by March 2027, with about $30 million estimated, of which about three-quarters falls in FY27 cash flow.
demand_pricing: Industry: GST on tyres cut from 28% to 18% for most categories (foam tyres 18% to 5%); management says demand momentum from the GST cut carried from Q3 into Q4 and Q1.
Input costs: crude about $107/bbl (about $65 at start of Q4), natural rubber about INR245/kg (from INR190/kg), and rupee at about INR94/$ (from about INR90).
Pricing: MRF reportedly took about 3-3.5% price hikes across segments; competitors' hikes are delayed and staggered.
Management expects demand moderation in Q1 as the 5-10% price hikes pass through, with progression by end-Q1 and into Q2.
US tariffs: on-road tyres (PCUV and truck-bus radial) at 25% plus about 4% base; OHT tariff reduced from 50% to 10%, with a refund process under court order being followed up.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 15% RM increase is reflected in current commodity prices, and how much more could come in the next 1-2 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 estimate of about 15% is based on inventory, orders and 3-month buying cover; replacement cost today could be higher. Visibility beyond Q1 depends on how the quarter unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative price increases in replacement and international, and whether the hikes are staggered?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement needs about 10% over March: about 5% taken by April and the balance staggered over May-June. OEM index hike is low single digit from 1 April and heavier from 1 July. International: 3-5% taken with another 5% announced, pass-through taking 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: CAMSO revenue ramp-up timing, FY28 production, and when double-digit margins are achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume and value increase only from H2 FY27 once customer interface moves to CEAT. Aftermarket grows first; OEM growth from FY28. Margin impact from FY28; the company will stick to the margins underlying the acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 volume growth and segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone volume grew close to 20% YoY in Q4; international in mid-20s and replacement and OEM in mid-teens to 20s.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and FY27 growth impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 15% of business, near zero in Q4 and not expected to recover fully. Q1 order base looks good excluding the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 consolidated capex and CAMSO upstream capex?
qa_highlights.answer: India ex-CAMSO capex INR1,350-1,400 crore. CAMSO upstream about $20-25 million in FY27 on top of that, with the total upstream estimate about $30 million.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive price hike scenario and demand outlook for H2 after a 10% price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are coming through staggered and delayed at some competitors. Truck-bus replacement may slow to low single digit but not turn negative. PCR is expected to improve from 1-2% to 3-5%. 2-wheeler stays at single to high single-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost outlook and sharp rise in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about INR3,000 crore for three quarters and will be held near that in Q1. Other income of INR62.5 crore includes hedging gains and CAMSO royalty and is not sustainable; previous-quarter average is the right base.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days, consolidated working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone finished goods inventory at 24-27 days; March is the seasonal low. Consolidated inventory rose on CAMSO raw materials (over INR200 crore extra) held as supply security. Standalone working capital rose INR108 crore QoQ and INR139 crore in FY26, with GST credit balances of about INR120 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: Q1 cost up about 15%, possibly near 20% by end-Q1, with only half the price increase passed through so far, which risks margin compression.
Demand moderation from 5-10% replacement price hikes, especially in truck-bus radial, with H2 comparisons against a strong base.
West Asia conflict and fuel price path: Middle East is about 15% of international business; geopolitical risk premium and physical supply constraints on inputs.
CAMSO transition: margins and revenue ramp depend on taking over sales and purchase value chain; FY27 margins may fluctuate.
Working capital: standalone working capital turned positive (INR108 crore) and needs to return to negative; about INR120 crore of GST credits stuck in two states.
Leverage: debt may rise above INR3,000 crore after Q1 as capex steps up; the company says it will keep leverage ratios responsible.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and demand momentum, but cautious on Q1 FY27: management repeatedly called the raw material and geopolitical situation dynamic and said it will calibrate capex and pricing quarter by quarter.
key_quotes: So, price increase is an imperative. In OEM, the price increase comes with a lag. So 1st July will get a big increase.
We need to take overall 10% vis-a-vis March, in replacement. Out of that, about 5% can be considered as taken already between March and April.
We'll still stick to the underlying margins based on which we acquired the business.
We would be frugal and careful in quarter 1, considering current situation, and we'll scale up as we go by, once things normalize.
So we expect moderation in demand, but it's not like… we don't expect a degrowth in truck bus radial tire even after a 10% price hike.

adds.what: CAMSO upstream facility (mixers and calenders), about $30 million estimated, ~3/4 in FY27 cash flow

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management guides Q1 FY27 raw material costs up ~15% (possibly ~20%), ~10% replacement price hikes, and expects demand moderation (no degrowth), with FY27 India capex of INR1,350-1,400 crore (about 25% above FY26) and CAMSO upstream ready by March 2027.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Raw material cost up about 15% in Q1 (possibly near 20% by end-Q1) against about 10% replacement price hikes, with management saying only a small portion can be offset by cost optimisation; Q4 standalone EBITDA margin was about 14.6%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 India capex of INR1,350-1,400 crore (about 25% above FY26's INR1,076 crore) and CAMSO upstream mixers and calenders ready by March 2027, though Q1 capex is limited to INR200-250 crore of mandatory spend.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone volume grew close to 20% YoY in Q4 and utilisation is 85-90%, but management expects demand moderation as 5-10% price hikes pass through, with truck-bus replacement slowing to low single digit.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 85-90% with planned utilisation of 90%-plus, and management says growth capex will be scaled up once conditions normalise, so further capex is likely to be guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on Q1 FY27 with raw material inflation of about 15% (possibly 20%) and a dynamic West Asia and fuel-price backdrop, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material inflation of about 15% with only about half of the price increase passed through so far, plus demand moderation and a strong H2 FY26 comparison base, creates margin and volume risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Product launches were not discussed in the brief.

rows.label: Replacement price hike of about 10% vs March
rows.why: About 5% already taken by April with the balance of about 5% staggered over May-June; pass-through takes 30-45 days in international.

rows.label: CAMSO customer interface takeover to about 90%
rows.why: Volume and value uplift only from H2 FY27 once interface moves to CEAT, with CAMSO margin impact from FY28 and transition complete by March 2027.

rows.label: Standalone working capital back to negative
rows.why: Standalone working capital rose INR108 crore QoQ to positive and about INR120 crore of GST credits are stuck in two states; management has not given a timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery and demand momentum, but cautious on Q1 FY27 raw material inflation, Middle East exposure and pass-through pace; analysts pressed on the 15% RM estimate beyond Q1, price hike cumulative, and CAMSO ramp.

oneOffs.what: INR62.5 crore other income in the quarter includes hedging gains and CAMSO royalty and is not sustainable; this is below the revenue line and affects profit, not revenue growth
GST cut on tyres from 28% to 18% for most categories lifted demand in Q4 and carried into Q1; a policy tailwind rather than a one-time item, but it flatters the Q4 growth rate

quality.why: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue grew 18.2% with volume up close to 20% YoY, so growth is mainly volume-driven and organic, but the GST rate cut is a policy tailwind that flatters the growth rate, and the INR62.5 crore other income (hedging gains and CAMSO royalty, which management says is not sustainable) flatters profit rather than revenue.
